title: Two Concepts of Liberty: An Inaugural Lecture Delivered Before the University of Oxford on 31 October 1958
subtitle: An Inaugural Lecture Delivered Before the University of Oxford on 31 October 1958
author: Isaiah Berlin
description: "This lecture insisted upon negative liberty as the political complement to the human capacity for free choice, and made matching metaphysical claims: the nature of being, and especially the conflicts amongst values, were inconsistent with totalitarian claims. Berlin, arguing along this line, provided an account of the perversion of positive liberty into a warrant for such claims, discussed nationalism, and emphasized the value‐pluralism, now linked so frequently with his name"--Taken from Oxford Scholarship Online.
